papers.sourceCoverage: Primary PDF pp. 1-16: abstract, methods, Tables 1-10, Figures 1-3, results, discussion and limitations.
papers.rationale: Cross-sectional survey of 90 Polish amateur/professional male footballers, assessing eating-disorder risk and body esteem. The participant questionnaire mentions chronic conditions only as background; it reports no injury or illness surveillance outcome, usable denominator, incidence, burden, severity, mechanism, diagnosis or location family compatible with Tabs 1-10.
papers.blankStructuredFamilies: All results are EAT-26/BES, BMI, diet and social-media measures; no injury/illness structured family is supported.

papers.sourceCoverage: Primary PDF pp. 1-17: abstract, methods, Table 1, Table 2, Figures 1-3, results, discussion and conclusion.
papers.rationale: Age- and education-matched cross-sectional comparison of 214 elite male soccer players and 110 non-athlete controls using BDI-II/BAI and suicidal-ideation measures. It is a mental-health symptom study, not injury/illness surveillance; no GBI injury/illness numerator, denominator, exposure, incidence, burden, severity, mechanism, diagnosis or location value is reported.
papers.blankStructuredFamilies: Psychometric symptom/severity data and neural-network classification do not map to the GBI injury/illness schema.

papers.sourceCoverage: Primary PDF pp. 1-12: abstract, methods, Tables 1-7, Figure 1, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion.
papers.rationale: Chinese adolescent football-engagement latent-profile study (n=1,659) with self-esteem and depression-score outcomes. The methods explicitly exclude adolescents with sports-related injuries; all reported outcomes are engagement/psychometric measures, with no injury or illness surveillance value for Tabs 1-10.
papers.blankStructuredFamilies: No player injury/illness outcome, numerator, exposure, incidence, burden, severity, mechanism, tissue/type or location family is reported.

papers.sourceCoverage: Primary PDF pp. 1-8: abstract, methods, Tables 1-2, Figures 1-3, results, discussion and limitations.
papers.rationale: The survey reports 295 prior-six-month, self-reported time-loss injuries among 668 ECNL respondents plus type, location, mechanism and duration distributions. It reports no athlete-/match-/training-exposure total, time-based rate, or defensible inputs for a GBI denominator. Headcount and six-month percentage are not an accepted at-risk denominator, and exposure must not be back-calculated; the record is therefore flagged for no exposure rather than extracted.
papers.blankStructuredFamilies: Direct injury characteristics were swept but intentionally unstaged because the necessary at-risk denominator is absent; no count, rate, burden, severity or structured row is applied.

papers.sourceCoverage: Primary PDF pp. 1-10: abstract, methods, Tables 1-2, results, discussion, recommendations and conclusion.
papers.rationale: Australian A-Leagues cross-sectional mental-health survey of 313 men and 240 women. A dichotomous self-report of a severe musculoskeletal injury in the prior six months is only a regression covariate (32%/33%); the primary results are mental-health symptom prevalence, with no compatible injury surveillance count/rate/exposure, structured diagnosis/location, burden or severity payload.
papers.blankStructuredFamilies: Mental-health questionnaire prevalence and injury-association odds ratios do not support Tabs 1-10 injury/illness fields.
